spec: §3.5, last two rows — 300 KB initial, 250 KB per route chunk
measure: gzip KiB, as the bundler and the browser both report transfer size
note: scripts/check-bundle-budget.mjs reads this file. The gate fails when the
file is absent, when the build produces a target this file does not
declare, and when this file declares a target the build does not produce.
Raise a number here only with the measurement that justifies it.

initialNote: 310, not 300: measured 2026-09-07 on feat/platform-parity-wave (PR #823).
main's admin initial set was 295.3 KiB gzip; the wave's 300.3 KiB is that
plus 4.9 KiB of src/shared/i18n/en.json, which grew from 52.8 to 57.7 KiB
gzip with the toolkit catalogue, support assistant, Inventory, Settings
parity and lifecycle strings. The admin entry ships the whole catalogue
(one bundle, no namespace split — see shared/i18n/README.md), so every
app-side string lands in admin's initial set. Splitting the catalogue
per entry is the fix that brings this back to 300; until then the
budget records the measured cost rather than hiding it behind an
allowlist.
Own line, not folded into 'app' (PREAMBLE decision 7): a separate Vite
mode with its own dependency set (react + react-dom, minisearch, the
MDX-compiled content/component tree; no MUI). 200 (measured 156.6 KiB
gzip on the four W1a placeholder pages, 2026-09-08) did not survive the
real content merge: `content-registry.ts` imports every `content/**/*.mdx`
with `{ eager: true }` (its own header explains why — a handful of
placeholder pages, not a real site), so all 126 pages the embedded-docs
W5 merge landed (2026-09-08) compile into the entry's one JS chunk.
Measured 351.2 KiB gzip on that merge; 400 gives headroom for the
in-flight screenshot batches (embedded-docs W4a) before this needs
raising again. The real fix is switching `content-registry.ts` from
`eager: true` to a per-slug lazy `import()` keyed off `router.ts`'s
current slug, which would move most of this into routeChunkKB instead
of initialKB — out of scope for a content-merge unit, tracked as a
follow-up.
`mermaid` itself does NOT count here: Mermaid.tsx dynamic-imports it,
so its ~140 KiB gzip parser chunk (plus one further chunk per diagram
type it lazy-loads) lands in routeChunkKB below, not the initial set —
confirmed by index.html carrying no <link rel=modulepreload> for it.
